narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated an 82% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. This is a high-risk prediction, not a certainty, so it still implies about an 18% chance of passing. Your gender and race were not used in this prediction.

The strongest reason was your third-year class standing. You were in decile 1, while accepted students averaged near decile 6, and this factor pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your LSAT score was the second most influential factor: at 22.5 versus an accepted average of about 37.2, it also pushed toward failure. The third factor, your undergraduate GPA, was 2.70 versus an accepted average of 3.23. Among the top three factors, GPA was the only one that pushed toward passing, even though it remains below the admitted-student average.

To improve your chances, focus on what you can change most directly: prepare intensively to retake the LSAT, seek academic advising or tutoring to address your third-year class performance, and ask admissions staff what evidence would strengthen a future application. Consider delaying reapplication until you can show improved test scores and academic preparation, and provide context for any circumstances behind your record.
